A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SenseNova-SI research. The supplied text, figures, tables, and supplementary material support reliable comparison. v1 ends with references; v3 adds Appendices A–H.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations, scaling experiments, shortcut and CoT analyses, and simulated robotic-manipulation results in Section 5.

after.justification: v3 retains those original results and adds single-dataset experiments, general-capability evaluations, detailed benchmark results, and case studies.

M1.justification: The foundation-model architectures, data-centric training approach, and three CoT schemes remain unchanged. Appendix B elaborates the existing data-curation and CoT procedures; it does not establish a change to the implemented method.

E1.justification: Appendix E/Table 8 substantially broadens general-capability evaluation beyond MMBench-En by adding MMStar, AI2D scientific-diagram reasoning, and OCRBench text recognition. The original spatial benchmarks, manipulation task, and training-source coverage remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds Gemini-3-Pro-Preview as an evaluated comparator on all five spatial benchmarks. The previously reported comparator set is retained; the appendix largely provides further results for existing comparators.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds dataset-isolated training controls for ten InternVL3-8B variants. Table 10 additionally reports EASI-reproduced VST MMSI results alongside the paper-sourced aggregates retained in Table 1. The main training budget, optimizer, learning rate, and frame settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 6 substantially extends the earlier narrow single-source transfer examples into systematic training-source ablations. Appendices F and H add manipulation and CoT success/failure case studies, exposing recognition, execution-precision, and reasoning-consistency problems. The original robustness analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions describe Figure 1's bands as ±0.5 standard deviation across benchmark subtasks; Appendix A repeats this practice. v3 adds no repeated-run counts, seeds, significance tests, or new uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The original main-table scores remain, but Tables 6–13 add extensive ablation, scaling, general-capability, and subtask results. Gemini-3-Pro-Preview scores 45.2 on MMSI versus SenseNova-SI InternVL3-8B's 43.3. Some new aggregates conflict with Table 1, including MindCube's 41.2 versus 41.8 for SenseNova-SI InternVL3-2B; these are not established performance revisions.

T1.justification: Neither version develops theoretical results or proofs. The new frame-selection pseudocode and visualization-normalization explanation document procedures without establishing substantive changes to mathematical reasoning, assumptions, or formal properties.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: spatial data scaling, improved spatial performance, general-capability retention, emerging transfer, shortcut resistance, limited CoT benefits, and downstream utility. Additional evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix H introduces explicit hypotheses about CoT error accumulation and restrictive verbal supervision. Appendix F identifies object-recognition and manipulation-precision failure conditions. Appendices C and E add discussion of mixture balancing and general-task declines, materially extending the interpretation and limitations beyond v1.

D1.justification: Appendices A, B, and F newly document benchmark-to-capability mappings, annotation processing, filtering and sampling, overlap-controlled frame selection, detailed CogMap construction, and the robot's action interface and full prompt. These substantially improve implementation transparency; the existing code and model access links are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds references supporting MMStar, AI2D, OCRBench, and Gemini 3 Pro. Section 2's positioning around spatial data curation versus 3D-expert architectures remains essentially unchanged. The additional VLM-3R reference duplicates an already cited work.

P1.justification: The main narrative remains nearly verbatim, with localized wording and header edits. However, Appendices A–H substantially expand the exposition of existing work, developing brief descriptions into organized, stepwise accounts of data curation, CoT construction, and embodied-agent operation.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 6–13, Figures 5–8, an algorithm block, and detailed prompt/output displays. New visuals include annotated manipulation failures and CoT traces. Existing Figure 3 moves from page 7 to page 8, Figure 2 is resized with a clarified caption, and Table 1 gains a comparator row.

improvement.justification: v1 only sketches the central data-curation pipeline and robot interface, and tests general-capability retention mainly through MMBench-En. v3 substantially improves auditability through procedural details, training-source controls, broader evaluations, and explicit failure cases. These gains outweigh remaining reporting problems: Table 7's base-model ViewSpatial score conflicts with Table 1, and the retained general-capability claims insufficiently acknowledge declines such as InternVL3-8B's AI2D score falling from 85.2 to 79.0 after spatial training.
